tagline: One of the largest homebuilders in the United States
hero_kpi_rationale: Home deliveries is the key indicator of Lennar's operational performance and market share in the residential construction sector, directly reflecting housing demand and production capacity.

kpis.name: Home Deliveries
kpis.explanation: Number of homes delivered by the company
kpis.description: The company delivered 82,583 homes in 2025, up 3% compared to 80,210 homes in 2024
kpis.signal: Housing demand remains strong despite challenging market conditions and margin compression

kpis.name: Total Revenues
kpis.explanation: Consolidated total revenue of the company
kpis.description: Total revenue amounted to $34.2 billion in 2025, down 3% from $35.4 billion in 2024
kpis.signal: Revenue declined due to lower average selling prices, partially offset by increased delivery volume

kpis.name: Home Sales Revenues
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from home sales (Homebuilding segment)
kpis.description: Home sales revenue totaled $32.1 billion in 2025, down 5% from $33.8 billion in 2024
kpis.signal: Home sales revenue represents 94% of consolidated revenue and reflects lower average selling prices

kpis.name: Average Sales Price
kpis.explanation: Average selling price of delivered homes
kpis.description: The average selling price of homes was $391,000 in 2025, down 8% from $423,000 in 2024
kpis.signal: The 8% decline in average selling price reflects challenging market conditions and increased buyer incentives

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Gross margin on home sales as a percentage
kpis.description: Gross margin on home sales was 17.7% in 2025, compared to 22.3% in 2024
kpis.signal: The 450 basis point gross margin compression reflects lower revenue per square foot and higher land costs, partially offset by construction cost reductions

kpis.name: Net Earnings
kpis.explanation: Net income attributable to Lennar Corporation
kpis.description: Net income attributable to Lennar was $2.1 billion in 2025, down 46% from $3.9 billion in 2024
kpis.signal: Net income declined 46% due to margin compression and a $156.1 million impairment charge related to the Millrose exchange transaction

kpis.name: Selling, General and Administrative Ratio
kpis.explanation: Selling, general and administrative expenses as a percentage of home sales revenue
kpis.description: SG&A expenses represented 8.3% of home sales revenue in 2025, compared to 7.3% in 2024
kpis.signal: The SG&A ratio increased by 100 basis points due to lack of leverage on lower revenues and higher marketing and sales expenses

kpis.name: Financial Services Operating Earnings
kpis.explanation: Operating income from the Financial Services segment
kpis.description: Operating income from the Financial Services segment was $609.9 million in 2025, up 6% from $574.2 million in 2024
kpis.signal: The Financial Services segment reported growth in operating profit driven by higher profit per locked mortgage loan

risks.title: Housing demand affected by macroeconomic factors
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned first in risk factors, the language is strong ('materially adversely affect', 'significantly adversely affected'). The impact on employment, inflation and interest rates is presented as a constant concern for the sector. High sector weighting.

risks.title: Impact of inflation on profitability and costs
risks.score_rationale: Inflation is explicitly cited as negatively affecting margins ('reduced our profit margins') and increasing costs ('cost of capital, labor and materials can increase'). The language is direct and the impact on profitability is clear. Sector-weighted.

risks.title: Rising mortgage interest rates
risks.score_rationale: This risk is detailed with high intensity. The MD&A notes customers 'hesitant and limited by what they could afford to purchase' and that the moderate decline in mortgage rates in Q4 did not stimulate demand. It is presented as a major factor affecting affordability and demand. Sector-weighted.

risks.title: Reputation and negative publicity risks
risks.score_rationale: The text emphasizes brand importance ('dependent upon the reputation') and consequences of negative publicity ('could hurt our reputation', 'adversely affect our business'). The potential impact on sales and profits is clear. The speed of dissemination via social media is noted.

risks.title: Competition risks in homebuilding and financial services
risks.score_rationale: This risk is presented as a 'highly competitive' condition affecting multiple business segments ('homebuilding, mortgage lending, home rentals'). Impact on pricing, margins and resource acquisition is mentioned. Sector-weighted.

risks.title: Litigation and warranty claims risks
risks.score_rationale: The risk of warranty and construction defect claims is explicitly mentioned ('warranty and construction defect claims'). Potential insurance shortfalls and rising costs are highlighted. The language indicates serious concern.

risks.title: International conflicts and supply chain disruptions
risks.score_rationale: International conflicts are cited as potential causes of 'market disruptions', 'volatility in commodity prices' and 'supply chain interruptions'. While direct impact is currently limited, the potential for disruptions is emphasized. Sector-weighted.

ai_positioning.summary: Lennar Corporation does not mention artificial intelligence in its 10-K/20-F filing. The information provided focuses on the company's financial and operational aspects without addressing emerging technologies such as AI. However, the MD&A references technological advancements affecting future employment.
